core.title: Cover every presentation component with a smoke browser spec named after its product capability
core.given: A component playing the presentation role (an artifact of one of the profile's presentation kinds, at the presentation role's location), belonging to a product capability (the bounded product slice its path names).
core.when: The component is added or changed, or the coverage check reports it as uncovered.
core.then: Ensure this component is covered by a smoke browser spec whose path names the component's product capability.
prefer: Add a smoke browser spec whose file name contains the product capability, placed where the stack puts its e2e tests.
Make it a real browser spec — of the stack's e2e-test file kind, run by the stack's test runner, or a test file that declares its user-system-flow/journey binding — so a misnamed one is still judged.
avoid: Relying on structural or unit tests as coverage — they stay green while the rendered feature is blank.
Counting a unit test that merely mentions a journey URN in a string as a browser spec.
Naming a smoke spec without the product capability, so coverage cannot be attributed.
Treating an existing capability-named spec as covering every component in the product capability without it actually covering this one.
unless: The component is in a vendored or generated tree — never scanned; the exact classification of which trees count is owned by this rule's check in each realization, not by the stack-wide never-scanned list.
The component does not play the presentation role — out of scope.
core.why: Structural tests stay green while a rendered feature is blank; only rendering it in a browser proves it appears.
evidence: For every component playing the presentation role, a smoke browser spec whose path contains the product capability name covers it.
The coverage check reports no uncovered presentation component.
verification: Coverage is judged per component: the observer must establish, per presentation component, that a smoke browser spec naming its product capability actually covers it; the mere existence of a capability-named spec is not sufficient.

What counts as a browser spec comes from the profile: an e2e-test file kind run by the stack's test runner, or a test file that declares a user-system-flow/journey binding; a unit test that merely mentions a journey URN in a string is not a browser spec.
Scan scope: only the presentation role's component kinds, at the presentation role's location; anything not playing the presentation role is out of scope.

Vendored and generated trees are never scanned; this rule's check owns the exact classification of which trees count as vendored or generated. That concrete list is a realization detail and is deliberately not the stack-wide never-scanned list, so the exception is neither widened (by adopting the stack-wide list) nor dropped.
The concrete detector, validator and finding identifiers of this check are realization details of each stack's implementation.

values: presentation component not covered by a smoke browser spec naming its product capability

fires: A new component is added under the presentation role and no smoke browser spec path names its product capability.
A capability-named smoke browser spec already exists, but a newly added or previously uncovered component in that product capability is not covered by it.
A presentation component exists and the only test touching its product capability is a unit test that mentions a journey URN in a string.
The coverage check reports a presentation component not covered by a smoke browser spec naming its product capability.
doesNotFire: The component does not play the presentation role (it lives outside the presentation role's location).
The component is in a vendored or generated tree (never scanned).

neutralityNotes: 'SMOKE' is kept as the stack-neutral ATDD test-depth label (cf. urn.smoke_acceptance), and 'product capability'/'journey URN' are shared structure-profile vocabulary, so the core uses them freely. Everything concrete — component suffixes, the presentation location, the product capability path derivation, the e2e location and suffix, the runner and the header-comment binding markers — moved into profileRequirements; no key was missing from vocabulary.yaml. The detector/validator/finding ids and the concrete example path remain bunOnly. The exact four-tree exclusion set (node_modules, dist, build, _generated) is owned by this rule's checker, not by the stack-wide never-scanned list (which also includes .git and repository-configured excludes): per the closed vocabulary, that checker-owned classification is preserved as deference in the core's verification, with the concrete list in bunOnly — so instantiating the core with the Bun realization reproduces exactly bun.json's scan scope, neither widened by the stack-wide list nor weakened by dropping the exception.
